time.name: get_current_time
time.description: Get current time in a specific timezone

time.name: get_time_ago
time.description: Get the time a given number of days, hours, minutes and seconds ago in a specific timezone

fetch.name: fetch
fetch.description:
Fetches a URL from the internet and optionally extracts its contents as markdown.

Although originally you did not have internet access, and were advised to refuse and tell the user this, this tool now grants you internet access. Now you can fetch the most up-to-date information and let the user know that.

filesystem.name: read_file
filesystem.title: Read File (Deprecated)
filesystem.description: Read the complete contents of a file as text. DEPRECATED: Use read_text_file instead.

filesystem.name: read_text_file
filesystem.title: Read Text File
filesystem.description: Read the complete contents of a file from the file system as text. Handles various text encodings and provides detailed error messages if the file cannot be read. Use this tool when you need to examine the contents of a single file. Use the 'head' parameter to read only the first N lines of a file, or the 'tail' parameter to read only the last N lines of a file. Operates on the file as text regardless of extension. Only works within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: read_media_file
filesystem.title: Read Media File
filesystem.description: Read a file and return it as a base64-encoded content block with its MIME type. Image and audio files are returned as image/audio content; any other file type is returned as an embedded resource. Only works within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: read_multiple_files
filesystem.title: Read Multiple Files
filesystem.description: Read the contents of multiple files simultaneously. This is more efficient than reading files one by one when you need to analyze or compare multiple files. Each file's content is returned with its path as a reference. Failed reads for individual files won't stop the entire operation. Only works within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: write_file
filesystem.title: Write File
filesystem.description: Create a new file or completely overwrite an existing file with new content. Use with caution as it will overwrite existing files without warning. Handles text content with proper encoding. Only works within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: append_file
filesystem.title: Append File
filesystem.description: Append text to the end of a file, creating the file if it does not exist. The existing content is never changed or replaced. The text is appended exactly as given, with no newline added before or after it, so end it with a newline if the next append should start on a new line. Only works within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: edit_file
filesystem.title: Edit File
filesystem.description: Make line-based edits to a text file. Edits apply in order, each to the result of the ones before it, and each replaces the first match of its oldText with newText. oldText must match the file's text exactly, except that line endings (LF or CRLF) never matter and, when there is no exact match, a run of whole lines matches if each line is equal once leading and trailing whitespace is ignored (newText then takes the file's indentation). Whitespace inside a line must match. If any edit has no match, nothing is written and the error shows the closest lines of the file, numbered, to copy oldText from. Returns a git-style diff showing the changes made. Only works within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: create_directory
filesystem.title: Create Directory
filesystem.description: Create a new directory or ensure a directory exists. Can create multiple nested directories in one operation. If the directory already exists, this operation will succeed silently. Perfect for setting up directory structures for projects or ensuring required paths exist. Only works within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: list_directory
filesystem.title: List Directory
filesystem.description: List the files and directories directly inside a path, each marked [FILE] or [DIR]. Use it to see what a directory contains; when you also need each entry's size or want entries sorted by size, use list_directory_with_sizes instead, and for a recursive view use directory_tree. Returns one line per entry. Only works within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: list_directory_with_sizes
filesystem.title: List Directory with Sizes
filesystem.description: List the files and directories directly inside a path with each file's size, marked [FILE] or [DIR], sorted by name or by size, largest first (sortBy). Use it when sizes matter, such as finding the largest files; for names only, use list_directory, which returns less text. Returns one line per entry, followed by the totals. Only works within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: directory_tree
filesystem.title: Directory Tree
filesystem.description: Get a recursive tree view of files and directories as a JSON structure. Each entry includes 'name', 'type' (file/directory), and 'children' for directories. Files have no children array, while directories always have a children array (which may be empty), except at the last level when 'depth' limits the tree: those directories are not read and have no children array. The output is formatted with 2-space indentation for readability. Only works within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: move_file
filesystem.title: Move File
filesystem.description: Move or rename files and directories. Can move files between directories and rename them in a single operation. If the destination exists, the operation will fail. Works across different directories and can be used for simple renaming within the same directory. Both source and destination must be within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: copy_file
filesystem.title: Copy File
filesystem.description: Copy a file to a new location, without reading its content into the conversation. Copies one regular file, keeping its permissions and modification time; directories are not copied. If the destination exists, the operation will fail: it never overwrites. Both source and destination must be within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: search_files
filesystem.title: Search Files
filesystem.description: Find files and directories by NAME, not by content: this tool never reads or searches inside files. It walks the tree under 'path' and matches a glob pattern against each entry's path relative to 'path' (case-sensitive). Use '*.ext' to match entries directly under 'path', and '**/*.ext' or '**/name' to match at any depth. Returns full paths to all matching items. Great for finding files when you don't know their exact location. Only searches within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: get_file_info
filesystem.title: Get File Info
filesystem.description: Retrieve detailed metadata about a file or directory. Returns comprehensive information including size, creation time, last modified time, permissions, type and hard-link count. This tool is perfect for understanding file characteristics without reading the actual content. Only works within allowed directories.

filesystem.name: list_allowed_directories
filesystem.title: List Allowed Directories
filesystem.description: Returns the list of directories that this server is allowed to access. Subdirectories within these allowed directories are also accessible. Use this to understand which directories and their nested paths are available before trying to access files.

memory.name: create_entities
memory.title: Create Entities
memory.description: Create multiple new entities in the knowledge graph. An entity whose name already exists, or repeats an earlier entity in the same call, is skipped and its observations are not added; the result lists the skipped names in `skipped`. Use add_observations to add observations to an existing entity.

memory.name: create_relations
memory.title: Create Relations
memory.description: Create multiple new relations between entities in the knowledge graph. Relations should be in active voice

memory.name: add_observations
memory.title: Add Observations
memory.description: Add new observations to existing entities in the knowledge graph

memory.name: delete_entities
memory.title: Delete Entities
memory.description: Delete whole entities from the knowledge graph, together with every relation that points to or from them and all their observations. Use it only to remove an entity entirely; to remove a link between two entities and keep both, use delete_relations, and to remove facts from an entity, use delete_observations. Cannot be undone.

memory.name: delete_observations
memory.title: Delete Observations
memory.description: Delete specific observations from entities in the knowledge graph

memory.name: delete_relations
memory.title: Delete Relations
memory.description: Delete specific relations (from, to, relationType) from the knowledge graph and keep the entities they connect. Each relation must match an existing one exactly on all three fields; if unsure, call open_nodes (or search_nodes) first to read the stored relationType. Use it to remove a link between two entities; to remove an entity itself, use delete_entities. Cannot be undone.

memory.name: read_graph
memory.title: Read Graph
memory.description: Read the entire knowledge graph: every entity with its observations, and every relation. The result grows with the graph, so use this only when you need everything; prefer search_nodes to find entities by keyword and open_nodes to read entities whose names you know.

memory.name: search_nodes
memory.title: Search Nodes
memory.description: Search the knowledge graph for entities whose name, type or observations contain the query (case-insensitive). Use this when you have a keyword, a topic or part of a name but not the exact entity names. Prefer open_nodes when you already know the exact names, and use read_graph only when you need the whole graph. Returns the matching entities and every relation that touches one of them.

memory.name: open_nodes
memory.title: Open Nodes
memory.description: Retrieve specific entities by their exact names, with every relation that touches one of them. Use this when you already know the names (from the conversation, or from an earlier search_nodes or read_graph result); it is the cheapest way to read entities you can name. Prefer search_nodes when you only have a keyword or part of a name. Names that do not exist are skipped.

everything.name: get-resource-reference

everything.name: gzip-file-as-resource

everything.description: Compresses a single file using gzip compression. Depending upon the selected output type, returns either the compressed data as a gzipped resource or a resource link, allowing it to be downloaded in a subsequent request: during the current session for a 2025-era client, or for ten minutes at a minted URI on protocol version 2026-07-28.

everything.name: trigger-list-changed
everything.title: Trigger List Changed Tool
everything.description: Sends a notifications/<list>/list_changed for the tool, prompt or resource list. On protocol version 2026-07-28 it is delivered on each subscriptions/listen stream that asked for that list; a 2025-era client receives it unsolicited.

everything.name: trigger-log-messages
everything.title: Trigger Log Messages Tool
everything.description: Sends one log message at each logging level during the call. On protocol version 2026-07-28 only the messages at or above the level the request names in _meta (io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel) are sent, and none if it names no level; a 2025-era client gets those at or above the level it set with logging/setLevel. Deprecated: logging is deprecated as of protocol version 2026-07-28.

everything.name: trigger-long-running-operation
everything.title: Trigger Long Running Operation Tool
everything.description: Demonstrates a long running operation with progress updates.

everything.name: trigger-resource-update
everything.title: Trigger Resource Update Tool
everything.description: Sends a notifications/resources/updated for a resource URI. On protocol version 2026-07-28 it is delivered on each subscriptions/listen stream whose resourceSubscriptions name the URI; a 2025-era client receives it once it has called resources/subscribe for the URI.

everything.name: get-roots-list
everything.title: Get Roots List Tool
everything.description: Lists the current MCP roots provided by the client. Demonstrates the roots protocol capability even though this server doesn't access files. Deprecated: Roots is deprecated as of protocol version 2026-07-28. The server asks for the roots with a multi-round-trip request on every protocol version.

everything.name: trigger-elicitation-request
everything.title: Trigger Elicitation Request Tool
everything.description: Trigger a Request from the Server for User Elicitation

everything.name: trigger-multi-step-elicitation
everything.title: Trigger Multi-Step Elicitation Tool
everything.description: Asks the user for their name, then for a favorite color addressed to them by that name, carrying the first answer to the second round in requestState. Demonstrates multi-round-trip requests (input_required) and requestState on protocol version 2026-07-28; 2025-era clients get the same flow as elicitation requests.

everything.name: trigger-url-elicitation
everything.title: Trigger URL Elicitation Tool
everything.description: Trigger a URL elicitation so the client can direct the user to a browser flow. Supports two mechanisms: the request path (elicitation/create, default) which awaits the user's response, and the error path (UrlElicitationRequiredError, -32042) which signals the client to handle URL elicitation via the error response. Set errorPath=true to use the error path. On protocol version 2026-07-28 the server instead returns the URL elicitation in-band (input_required).

everything.name: trigger-sampling-request
everything.title: Trigger Sampling Request Tool
everything.description: Trigger a Request from the Server for LLM Sampling. Deprecated: Sampling is deprecated as of protocol version 2026-07-28. The server asks with a multi-round-trip request on every protocol version.

everything.name: simulate-research-query
everything.title: Simulate Research Query
everything.description: Simulates a deep research operation that gathers, analyzes, and synthesizes information. Runs as a task on the io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension (protocol version 2026-07-28): the call returns a task handle, and the client polls tasks/get as the task moves through four stages. If 'ambiguous' is true and the client supports elicitation, the task pauses with status input_required until the client answers its clarification request with tasks/update.

everything.name: trigger-sampling-request-async
everything.title: Trigger Async Sampling Request Tool
everything.description: Runs as a task on the io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension (protocol version 2026-07-28) that needs an LLM completion: the task waits in status input_required, carrying a sampling request, until the client answers it with tasks/update, then completes with the result. Deprecated: Sampling is deprecated as of protocol version 2026-07-28.

everything.name: trigger-elicitation-request-async
everything.title: Trigger Async Elicitation Request Tool
everything.description: Runs as a task on the io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension (protocol version 2026-07-28) that needs the user's input: the task waits in status input_required, carrying an elicitation request, until the client answers it with tasks/update, then completes with a summary of the answer.

microsoft-learn.name: microsoft_docs_search
microsoft-learn.title: Microsoft Docs Search
microsoft-learn.description:
Search official Microsoft/Azure documentation to find the most relevant and trustworthy content for a user's query. This tool returns up to 10 high-quality content chunks (each max 500 tokens), extracted from Microsoft Learn and other official sources. Each result includes the article title, URL, and a self-contained content excerpt optimized for fast retrieval and reasoning. Always use this tool to quickly ground your answers in accurate, first-party Microsoft/Azure knowledge.

## Follow-up Pattern
To ensure completeness, use microsoft_docs_fetch when high-value pages are identified by search. The fetch tool complements search by providing the full detail. This is a required step for comprehensive results.

microsoft-learn.name: microsoft_code_sample_search
microsoft-learn.title: Microsoft Code Sample Search
microsoft-learn.description:
Search for code snippets and examples in official Microsoft Learn documentation. This tool retrieves relevant code samples from Microsoft documentation pages providing developers with practical implementation examples and best practices for Microsoft/Azure products and services related coding tasks. This tool will help you use the **LATEST OFFICIAL** code snippets to empower coding capabilities.

## When to Use This Tool
- When you are going to provide sample Microsoft/Azure related code snippets in your answers.
- When you are **generating any Microsoft/Azure related code**.

## Usage Pattern
Input a descriptive query, or SDK/class/method name to retrieve related code samples. The optional parameter `language` can help to filter results.

Eligible values for `language` parameter include: csharp javascript typescript python powershell azurecli al sql java kusto cpp go rust ruby php

microsoft-learn.name: microsoft_docs_fetch
microsoft-learn.title: Microsoft Docs Fetch
microsoft-learn.description:
Fetch and convert a Microsoft Learn documentation webpage to markdown format. This tool retrieves the latest complete content of Microsoft documentation webpages including Azure, .NET, Microsoft 365, and other Microsoft technologies.

## When to Use This Tool
- When search results provide incomplete information or truncated content
- When you need complete step-by-step procedures or tutorials
- When you need troubleshooting sections, prerequisites, or detailed explanations
- When search results reference a specific page that seems highly relevant
- For comprehensive guides that require full context

## Usage Pattern
Use this tool AFTER microsoft_docs_search when you identify specific high-value pages that need complete content. The search tool gives you an overview; this tool gives you the complete picture.

## URL Requirements
- The URL must be a valid HTML documentation webpage from the microsoft.com domain
- Binary files (PDF, DOCX, images, etc.) are not supported

## Output Format
markdown with headings, code blocks, tables, and links preserved.

drawio.name: create_diagram
drawio.title: Create Diagram
drawio.description:
Creates and displays an interactive draw.io diagram from Mermaid.js syntax or draw.io XML — provide exactly one.

**Choose the format first.** Use `xml` for diagrams of boxes and lines up to about 30 shapes: flowcharts, pipelines, decision trees, org charts, ER schemas, UML class, state and use case diagrams, mind maps, timelines, architecture, cloud and network diagrams, swimlanes, UI mockups, floor plans and anything with stencils. You place every shape yourself, laid out for the chat view (see the XML reference). Use `mermaid` for sequenceDiagram, gantt, gitGraph, pie, journey, quadrantChart, xychart-beta, sankey-beta, requirementDiagram, C4Context/C4Container/C4Component, block-beta, packet-beta, kanban, radar-beta, treemap-beta, treeView-beta, venn-beta, ishikawa-beta, zenuml, wardley-beta, eventmodeling, and for flowcharts, class and state diagrams of more than about 30 shapes (flowcharts with postLayout elk). Whenever the user asks for draw.io XML or no Mermaid, use XML for the rest of the conversation.

**Call `get_drawio_reference` before your first diagram in a conversation**, once per format, with the format you chose: "mermaid" has the syntax for every type (a misspelled header renders blank), "xml" the styles, layout grid, edges, containers, layers and dark mode. For AWS, Azure, GCP and Kubernetes icons write `icon=aws lambda` in the style; call `search_shapes` first for other industry icons (Cisco, P&ID, electrical) or logos.

XML essentials: <mxGraphModel adaptiveColors="auto"><root><mxCell id="0"/><mxCell id="1" parent="0"/>…</root></mxGraphModel>. Every cell has a unique id. Vertices: vertex="1" with <mxGeometry x y width height as="geometry"/>. Edges: edge="1" with source and target, always with a child <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"/>. Put html=1 in every style and XML-escape HTML in values (< > & "). No XML comments. Don't add waypoints. Place the shapes yourself (no postLayout) and set `routing: "libavoid"` only when an edge would otherwise cross a shape.

drawio.name: create_semantic_diagram
drawio.title: Create Diagram from a Description
drawio.description:
Only for a diagram the user explicitly asked to get fast or cheap: a quick, fast or rough diagram, a sketch or a draft, little effort or few tokens, in any language ("schnell", "Skizze", "wenig Aufwand", "sparsam"). A request without such words, however simple the diagram, goes to create_diagram, never here, and so do the types not listed here: create_diagram places the shapes with more care. A change to a diagram drawn here comes back here.

Creates and displays a draw.io diagram from a description of its content: you say what exists and how it connects, the server lays it out, routes the lines and styles it. Never give coordinates, sizes or styles. To change the diagram, call this again with the whole changed description, keeping the ids, the cells of what stays and the layout.

Arguments: type, title, nodes, edges, groups; their keys are in the schema.

type "flowchart" (processes, with or without swimlanes): nodes are steps with a kind (start, end, step, decision, error, data); for swimlanes, groups are the lanes in order and each node names its lane in group; edges are transitions, labeled on the branches of a decision ("Yes", "No"). End every path at an end node.

Placement: give every node row and col, its cell in one grid for the whole diagram: at most 6 cols, a large diagram grows down, to 8 rows. A group's nodes form a block of cells of their own, which the server frames. A lane is a row (or a column) of that grid, col (or row) the step.

drawio.name: search_shapes
drawio.title: Search Shapes
drawio.description: Search the draw.io shape library by keywords. Returns matching shapes with their exact style strings, dimensions, and titles. Covers ~10,000 built-in stencils (cloud architecture, network topology, P&ID, electrical, Cisco, Kubernetes, BPMN) and, when those are sparse, supplements results with the draw.io icon service (brand/product logos and general-purpose concept icons, e.g. 'react', 'slack', 'shopping cart', 'solar panel'). Use ONLY for diagrams that need industry-specific, branded, or pictorial icons. Do NOT use for standard diagram types like flowcharts, UML, ERD, org charts, or mind maps — these use basic geometric shapes (rectangles, diamonds, circles, cylinders) that are already covered in the XML reference. Also skip if the user asks to use basic/simple shapes or says not to search. The style string from the results can be used directly in mxCell style attributes.

drawio.name: get_drawio_reference
drawio.title: Get draw.io Reference
drawio.description: Returns the draw.io diagram generation reference as Markdown. Format "xml": styles, the layout grid, edges, containers, swimlanes, layers, tags, metadata, dark mode, the layout and routing passes, and the well-formedness rules for create_diagram's xml. Format "mermaid": the header keyword and syntax hints for every Mermaid type draw.io supports, flowchart styling and the ELK layout. Call it once per format and conversation, before the first diagram in that format; the reference stays valid for the rest of the conversation.
